title: Sequencer safety protocol for multi-tool pipelines
creator: Elena Chen
description: Goal: implement a sequencer-level safety protocol that enables deterministic multi-tool chaining while preventing runaway recursion and ensuring streaming/tool-result integration preserves structured output contracts. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and rollout for: (1) a lightweight sequencer state machine that coordinates tool calls and streaming responses; (2) an injected-results protocol that attaches provenance + schema metadata to tool outputs; (3) runtime recursion/loop guards with quarantine and graceful fallback; and (4) compatibility hooks for older SDKs that expect non-streaming or flat output formats. Motivation: production traces show a small but increasing rate of tool-loop amplification when tool A calls tool B and then re-invokes tool A via result injection. We need deterministic bounds to protect SLOs and customer budgets while preserving developer ergonomics for tool/function calling and structured outputs.
technical_design: High-level approach: implement a sequencer per request session that tracks call graph depth, recent tool fingerprints, and a lightweight token/time budget. The sequencer enforces: (a) max effective recursion depth (configurable per workspace and per route); (b) tooling for detecting repeated call patterns via 128-bit prefix hash of tool name + normalized input; (c) streaming-aware result injection: when a tool produces an incremental stream, the sequencer buffers structured fragments and emits canonical schema-wrapped records to downstream tools; (d) compatibility layer: an opt-in shim that flattens schema-wrapped streaming fragments into legacy string-only outputs for older SDK versions. Implementation notes: add SequencerContext object (immutable snapshots for retries), introduce InjectedResult envelope with fields: schema_id, provenance_id, partial=true/false (stored as metadata headers for binary streaming), and introduce a RecursionQuarantine that records offending fingerprints and returns a controlled fallback token to the client. Backpressure: sequencer uses channel windows for streaming tool outputs and applies per-tool concurrency semaphores to avoid noisy neighbors. Telemetry: emit sequencer.trace events, recursion.quarantine_count, injected_result.schema_mismatch_count. Runtime changes limited to runtime-2.3; API contract changes behind a feature flag 'sequencer_v1' to allow gradual rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Sequencer enforces configurable max_depth and rejects additional recursive calls with 409/controlled fallback response
InjectedResult envelope is attached to all tool outputs when feature flag enabled and includes schema_id and provenance_id headers
Streaming tool outputs can be consumed by downstream tools without reassembly bugs; end-to-end integration test demonstrates stream->tool->stream flow preserving structured JSON records
Compatibility shim returns legacy flat output for SDKs <= 1.8 when workspace compatibility mode is enabled
Telemetry and dashboards show recursion.quarantine_count and no SLO regressions in canary (p99 latency increase < 5% at 95th percentile traffic)
testing_plan: Unit tests for SequencerContext snapshot/restore, hash-based fingerprint detection, and InjectedResult envelope serialization. Integration tests: (1) simulated multi-tool chain (ToolA -> ToolB -> ToolA) verifying quarantine triggers at configured depth; (2) streaming chain test with chunked JSON records and downstream consumer validating structured schema ids; (3) compatibility test for legacy SDK shim. Chaos test: fuzzed tool responses to ensure sequencer doesn't deadlock and falls back after budget exhaustion. Add e2e canary that routes 1% of production traffic with 'sequencer_v1' on and extra sampling for recursion traces.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; 2) Internal dogfood for Redwood Console and a few stable tenants for 1 week; 3) Canary: enable 'sequencer_v1' for 1% traffic for 48 hours with circuit monitoring and auto-disable on error thresholds; 4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% over two weeks, validating telemetry and customer impact dashboards; 5) Deprecation path: announce compatibility shim and schedule SDK bump guidance in release notes. Rollback: flip 'sequencer_v1' off and drain any quarantine state via background job.
notes: 2026-02-18 Elena Chen: Created ticket after observing two production incidents where chained tools re-entered the same tool with slightly different payloads causing token amplification and billing surprises.

2026-02-24 Marcus Li: Spike completed for fingerprinting scheme (64-bit Murmur + normalized input canonicalizer). Chose 128-bit prefix to reduce collision risk; added canonicalization rules for whitespace/ordering of JSON object keys.

2026-02-28 Design review (Ava Martinez): Agreed on InjectedResult envelope but requested that schema_id be optional and validation happen at consumption time to avoid hard failures for third-party tools.
2026-03-04 Security review kickoff (Rohit Patel): Raised question about provenance_id entropy and replay resistance. Action: use per-session UUIDv7 + HMAC suffix tied to workspace key.

2026-03-08 Marcus Li: Implemented sequencer snapshotting and basic quarantine logic in feature branch. Local integration tests passed for simple loops; failing intermittent timeout when downstream tool streams very slowly (open investigation).

2026-03-10 QA (Priya Srinivasan): Integration test showed schema_mismatch_count spikes when ToolB sends mixed string and JSON fragments; added stricter chunk-boundary checks and sanitizer in sequencer stream assembler.
2026-03-12 Marcus Li: Fixed stream assembler and added exponential backoff for quarantine retries. Preparing PR and will request informal review from runtime leads before full review.
